title: Only the sphere reads distance plainly: the plain first need fails on every flat torus but 26 and beyond a horizon on curved tilings
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: Without freezing, every loop of rings, pair of rings and Platonic network reads distance at every size, while flat and hyperbolic tilings hide it beyond a horizon set by ring and face sizes, so exactly 26 tori read it. The smallest regular map that fails, a 13-ring twisted square torus, reads it in its mirror image, so no criterion by type, genus, curvature or size decides finite maps.
